newsitem.title: USA: Dow says to license DJIA for investments.
newsitem.headline: Dow says to license DJIA for investments.

text.p: For the the first time in its 101-year history, Dow Jones & Co said Thursday it would license its Dow Jones Industrial Average, perhaps the most closely stock index in the world, for investment products.

Dow Jones said it licensed three exchanges to sell investment product based on the DJIA. The American Stock Exchange will offer an exchange-traded unit investment trust. The Chicago Board of Trade will offer trading in futures contracts and options on futures contracts; and the Chicago Board Options Exchange will offer trading in listed options contracts.
Dow said it expects DJIA products to begin trading some time in the fall. Dow Jones said it expects to award other DJIA licenses at a later date, but it did not provide details.
Also, Dow did not rule out deals on its other indices, like the transports and utilities.
It said the current license deals were subject to regulatory approval.
Dow said the deals would have a positive impact on financial results but declined to comment on whether the impact would be material.

"This is a historic event for Dow Jones & Company and for investors everywhere," said Peter Kann, chairman and chief executive officer. "Once these products are registered, investors will be able to invest using the same tool they now use to follow the stock market -- the Dow Jones Industrial Average. This significantly reinforces Dow Jones' position as the premier provider of global market information."
David E. Moran, president of Dow Jones Global Indexes, said the company decided that "increased sophistication" among investors "helped persuade us that now is the time" to introduce the products.
A unit investment trust is a variation of a mutual fund, with a fixed, unmanaged stock portfolio that is liquidated after a specified period of time.
The DJIA is comprised of 30 blue-chip U.S. stocks and is widely viewed as a barometer of the U.S. stock market. Introduced in 1896, the DJIA is the oldest continuing U.S. market index.
